descriptionChirho: An interjection or imperative calling someone to approach, move toward the speaker, or follow — functioning as a verbal command of summons. This is the dominant usage (8 of 9 occurrences), always directing motion toward the speaker or toward a designated goal. Multilingual glosses consistently render motion imperatives: Spanish 'ven' (come!), Arabic 'هَلُمَّ' / 'تَعَالَ' (come here!), Hindi 'आ' (come!), Korean '와서' (come and) / '오라' (come!), Swahili 'njoo' (come!). Attested in Jesus' calls to discipleship (Matt 19:21; Mark 10:21; Luke 18:22; John 11:43; Acts 7:3, 34; Rom 1:13; Rev 17:1; 21:9).

A temporal adverb meaning 'up to the present moment' or 'until now,' marking a point in time rather than directing physical motion. This is a rare usage (1 occurrence) that is semantically and syntactically distinct from the imperative sense. Multilingual glosses confirm the temporal reading: Spanish 'ahora' (now), Arabic 'الآنَ' (now/the present), Hindi 'अब' (now), Korean '지금' (right now/at this moment), Swahili 'sasa' (now/presently). Attested in Rom 1:13 (variant reading) or John 16:24 depending on textual tradition, where it marks temporal extent rather than spatial direction.
